Answer: D
Reason: The CT image (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined, patchy parenchymal consolidation in the left lower lobe with visible air bronchograms and a subpleural/peribronchial distribution. This radiographic appearance, combined with the clinical history of persistent infiltrates unresponsive to antibiotics, is characteristic of Bronchiolitis Obliterans Organizing Pneumonia (BOOP), also known as Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP).
